title: How to Get Clients in Construction
meta_description: How to get clients in construction: use the network you already have, fix your online presence, publish content worth reading, and follow up properly.
h1: How to Get Clients in Construction
hero_subtitle: A practical guide to filling the pipeline without waiting for the phone to ring.

intro.answer: The fastest source of new construction clients is almost always the network you already have. Most businesses go looking for strangers before they have finished asking the people who already know their work.

image.alt: A construction business owner meeting a prospective client

intro.roadmap: This guide covers the strategies that actually fill a pipeline: leveraging your network and referrals, optimising your online presence, using content marketing, delivering service worth talking about, and following up by email.

briefing.title: Start With the Network You Already Have
briefing.intro: In construction your network is a goldmine, and it is almost always underused. Past clients, suppliers, subcontractors and professional contacts all know what your work is like, which is the hardest thing to prove to anyone else.

panels.heading: How do you get clients in construction?
paragraphs: Start by tapping the relationships you already have rather than starting cold. A referral arrives pre-qualified and pre-trusted, which is why it converts at a rate no advert matches.

Then make sure someone checking you out afterwards finds something convincing. Most enquiries look you up before they call, and an out of date online presence quietly loses work you never knew you were in for.

panels.heading: Then build the other channels
paragraphs: In this order, because each one is cheaper than the one after it.
steps: Ask your existing network, deliberately rather than hoping.
Fix your online presence so it stands up to being checked.
Publish content that shows you know the work.
Deliver service worth mentioning, then ask for the mention.
Follow up by email, because most enquiries are not ready the first time.

review.label: Worth remembering
review.text: Exceptional service and follow-up is a client acquisition strategy, not an operations one. The job you deliver well this month is the enquiry you get next year.
